items.title: Re-vendor LibKa0s v1.71.0 from the local tag; record the unrecorded v1.69.0/v1.70.0 re-vendors in one span bundle
items.spec: Mechanical re-vendor per /dev-copilot:wow-revendor-libka0s conventions, non-interactive (OWNER_SCOPE 5). Source: the LOCAL tag v1.71.0 in ../LibKa0s (`git -C ../LibKa0s archive v1.71.0` or a temporary `git worktree add` of the tag, removed afterwards; never the LibKa0s working tree). (1) Replace libs/LibKa0s/ with the tag's LibKa0s/ payload whole and tests/_kit/ with the tag's testkit/ whole (delete-and-copy, never patch in place). (2) CLAUDE.md provenance line becomes exactly `Bundles [LibKa0s](https://github.com/tusharsaxena/LibKa0s) v1.71.0 (MIT).` in the same commit (tests/test_vendor_sync.lua reads it); the stale 'kit revision 35' in CLAUDE.md's Gate paragraph becomes 'kit revision 38'; the 'Fourteen of its majors are consumed' paragraph is re-checked against the tag (no major added in v1.71.0, so it should stand). (3) Kit 38 changes the --list Totals semantics (LK-01): regenerate docs/test-cases.md and make the README [Tests] badge equal the new Total. (4) docs/revendor/<date>-v1.71.0/ with 01_DELTA.md (line 1 exactly `Delta: LibKa0s v1.70.0 -> v1.71.0`; base taken from this repo's CLAUDE.md provenance line, v1.70.0; per-file LibStub minors: Env 2, Slash key 20.2, Widgets LineChart 3 / Autocomplete 2, OptionsIdList 4, kit 37 -> 38; which of the touched majors this addon consumes: Slash, Options/OptionsIdList and Env yes, WidgetsLineChart and WidgetsAutocomplete not called), 02_CANDIDATES.md (Kit.secret, ChartMath.ClipSegment and any other new surface listed as 'not adopted in this run' per OWNER_SCOPE 5; no interview, no GitHub issue), 05_SUMMARY.md. Note in 01_DELTA that Slash 20.2's ParseValue nan/inf refusal (LK-05) covers composed schema rows only; host parsing in core/SlashCommands.lua is CM-04's. (5) The span bundle for the two unrecorded re-vendors (CM-A-01, f8d2f3b and 74bcda1): docs/revendor/<date>-v1.69.0-v1.70.0/ with 01_DELTA.md whose line 1 is exactly `Delta: LibKa0s v1.69.0 -> v1.70.0 (span: v1.69.0 v1.70.0)`, base v1.68.1 stated in the body, naming the two commits and noting that WidgetsLineChart (new in v1.69.0) and WidgetsAutocomplete are not called by this addon; 05_SUMMARY.md with one line per tag: carried by the sweep, nothing adopted. Both bundles are frozen once committed. No addon code changes except what a red gate after the copy forces (if any red appears, stop and record it in the bundle; fix only if it is a mechanical consequence of the new payload).

items.title: Macro fingerprint is trusted only when the live account-wide macro still holds that body; deleted or overwritten KCM_* macros are rewritten
items.spec: modules/MacroManager.lua. New local `liveBody(macroName)`: `local idx = GetMacroIndexByName and GetMacroIndexByName(macroName)`; returns nil when idx is nil or 0, else the body from `GetMacroInfo(idx)` (third return); both are unprotected reads and are safe in combat. `alreadyApplied(state, pending, body, icon)` gains the macro name and returns true only when the fingerprint matches (state.lastBody == body and state.lastIcon == icon) AND `liveBody(macroName) == body` AND (pending == nil or pending.body == body). On a missing macro or a live body that differs (another profile/character wrote its own body to the account-wide macro, or the player deleted it), commitMacro falls through to the existing path: queueForCombat in combat, else doEdit (which creates a missing macro) and the macroState store. Do not compare the live icon (GetMacroInfo returns a texture, not the stored icon key). No change to macroState's shape, to InvalidateState or MarkAllStale. Mock: tests/wow_mock.lua must model GetMacroIndexByName/GetMacroInfo over its macro table (add if missing; it is at 1012 lines, so keep the addition small or put the helper in an existing support file). docs/macro-manager.md gains a paragraph: the fingerprint is a cache of the addon's own last write, macros are account-wide, so the live body is re-read before the 'unchanged' early-out; this is what makes README.md:127 and docs/scope.md:24 ('each character rewrites on arrival') true. ARCHITECTURE.md's macroState section names liveBody as a read (by function name, no line suffix).
items.steps:
1. Red first in tests/test_macromanager.lua (or tests/test_profiles.lua for the profile case): (a) profile A writes KCM_X with item 950001's body, the mock's account macro is overwritten with item 950002's body (simulating another character's profile), a pass with the same picks rewrites it to 950001; (b) the player deletes KCM_X, the next pass recreates it; (c) live body equal to the fingerprint still returns 'unchanged' and issues no EditMacro. Add '-- red under:' notes naming the removal of the liveBody comparison. Run `lua5.1 tests/run.lua`, see (a) and (b) fail.
2. Add liveBody and thread macroName into alreadyApplied.
3. Green gate. When the case count moves, regenerate docs/test-cases.md (`lua5.1 tests/run.lua --list > docs/test-cases.md`, CRLF) and bump the README [Tests] badge in the same commit (CLAUDE.md Static badges hard rule).
4. docs/macro-manager.md paragraph; ARCHITECTURE.md mention.
5. Commit `CM-01: ...`.

items.title: OnSpecChanged ignores groupmates' respecs and runs a discovery pass for the new spec before recomputing
items.spec: core/ConsumableMaster.lua KCM:OnSpecChanged becomes `function KCM:OnSpecChanged(event, unit)`. First line: `if unit and unit ~= "player" then return end` (before traceEvent, requestRecompute and the SPEC_CHANGED SendMessage; a nil unit passes, as the existing tests call it with none). Then traceEvent, then `runAutoDiscovery("spec_changed")` (the local defined above at :450, so no forward-declaration issue: confirm it is in scope at OnSpecChanged's definition), then requestRecompute("spec_changed") and the SPEC_CHANGED message as today. Discovery is filed per spec (discoverySpecKey reads SpecHelper.GetCurrent), so this fills the new spec's buckets with unseeded bag items before the recompute. docs/data-flow.md's PLAYER_SPECIALIZATION_CHANGED event row names the discovery pass and the player-only filter; ARCHITECTURE.md's Event Subscriptions row (by handler name) likewise.

items.title: /cm priority accepts only a positive item ID or s:<positive spell ID>; everything else prints the usage line
items.spec: core/SlashCommands.lua parsePriorityID(token): accept `^%d+$` with tonumber > 0 (an item ID) or `^[sS]:(%d+)$` with tonumber > 0 (a spell, returned through KCM.ID.AsSpell); return nil for anything else (0, 1.5, 0x10, 1e3, -20484, nan, inf, empty), so the existing usage line prints at all three callers (add, remove, move: the parsePriorityID call sites). This makes the slash door agree with the panel's Add-by-ID box (settings/CategoryAddByID.lua:213 already uses `text:match("^%d+$")`); if a shared helper is natural, put one strict numeric-ID parser on KCM.ID and have both call it, otherwise keep them separate and cite each other by function name. No change to stored data shapes. LK-05 (Slash ParseValue refuses nan/inf) is the library-side analogue for composed rows; this item is the host grammar.

items.title: Out-of-combat bar refresh scores each flyout candidate once: one scoreCache per MacroBar.Refresh threaded to Selector.ListAvailable
items.spec: modules/MacroBar.lua MB.Refresh: when not in combat, build one `local scoreCache = { fields = {} }` per refresh and pass it to `KCM.MacroBarFlyout.Apply(btn, c, scoreCache)`. modules/MacroBarFlyout.lua: FO.Apply(button, cfg, scoreCache) passes it to FO.Candidates(catKey, cfg, scoreCache), which calls `KCM.Selector.ListAvailable(catKey, nil, scoreCache)` (today nil). Callers that pass no cache keep the uncached path (Ranker.itemFields' contract, modules/Ranker.lua:78-96). The cache lives only for the one refresh (never stored on a module, so a later bag change is never served stale data). Scope note in the commit and in docs/performance.md: the review's 226 KB figure is a mock artifact (tests/wow_mock.lua's GetItemByID returns nil, so TooltipCache refetches), so the claim is one scoring pass (one itemFields fill) per candidate per refresh, not a byte figure; no perf number is quoted unless a scenario uses a mock that returns real tooltip lines.
